name: Frax USD
oneLiner: frxUSD is Frax's tokenized-T-bill-backed dollar, minted 1:1 by governance-approved custodians holding BUIDL, USTB, WTGXX, and other tokenized cash-equivalents.
collateral: Tokenized cash-equivalent reserves held by governance-approved enshrined custodians: BlackRock BUIDL (U.S. Treasuries/repos via Securitize), Superstate USTB (T-bills) and USCC (U.S. government securities), Centrifuge JTRSY (T-bills), WisdomTree WTGXX (U.S. government money market), Agora AUSD, and Circle USDC; each custodian mints and redeems frxUSD 1:1 against reserves they hold on-chain
pegMechanism: 1:1 mint and redemption through governance-approved enshrined custodians; each custodian holds provable on-chain reserves and can mint or burn frxUSD 1:1; redeemable from any custodian with available collateral

genius.issuerEntity: Financial Reserves and Asset Exploration Inc. (dba FRAX Inc)
genius.licensingRegulator: OCC (targeted; GENIUS Act nonbank PPSI pathway; no application on file as of 2026-06-07)
genius.notes: Frax governance passed FIP-430 (April 2025) and FIP-432 (July 2025) to prepare frxUSD for U.S. GENIUS Act payment-stablecoin charter compliance and formally transfer compliance and collateral management to FRAX Inc (formerly FinresPBC / Financial Reserves and Asset Exploration Inc.). The OCC digital-assets licensing application tracker (checked 2026-06-18) lists no pending application from Frax Finance, Financial Reserves and Asset Exploration Inc., or FRAX Inc. StableCharter.com categorizes status as 'PREPARING.' The GENIUS Act application framework itself remains in proposed-rule stage. authorizationStatus remains issuer-announced-intent — issuer intent is clear and well-documented but no official PPSI application has been filed. issuerPathway set to federal-qualified-nonbank reflecting the OCC nonbank PPSI route being pursued (not an IDI subsidiary, not foreign-registered); neither FIP explicitly names OCC but FRAX Inc. is a US nonbank entity with no state PPSI registration found, making the OCC federal nonbank pathway the only consistent federal route.

controls.label: frxUSD upgrade timelock
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25546949, all six frxUSD token/custodian ProxyAdmins returned this verified Compound-style timelock as owner. Its admin() was the 4-of-7 frxUSD owner/custodian admin Safe, pendingAdmin() was zero, and delay() was 86400 seconds; verified source requires the admin to queue upgrades and wait through the delay before execution.

controls.label: frxUSD owner/custodian admin Safe
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25546949, frxUSD token owner(), every listed custodian owner(), and the upgrade timelock admin() returned this Safe. On-chain Safe reads returned version 1.3.0, threshold 4, the seven listed owners, no enabled modules, zero guard, and zero moduleGuard.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25546949, the frxUSD token and all five custodian proxies published by Frax resolved distinct EIP-1967 implementations and ProxyAdmins. Every ProxyAdmin had identical verified runtime and owner() = 0xb898Ad2976b4d8f2E21521C9db16b7497825E503. That verified timelock had admin 0xfFFffF4F3baC444b2C0ecf2A1840d018bE783937, pendingAdmin zero, and a 86400-second delay. The same 4-of-7 Safe directly owned the token and every custodian, could raise their mint caps, and had no enabled modules, guard, or module guard. This establishes the complete published Ethereum token/custodian upgrade and mint-control chain; replacing mint-critical logic requires the Safe-controlled 24-hour timelock.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: frxUSD uses or is linked to LayerZero/OFT-style cross-chain token infrastructure. Because OFT/adapter routes depend on external messaging, endpoint configuration, and lock/mint or burn/mint token contracts outside issuer-native redemption alone, Pharos scores the reviewed route as external lock/mint.
